setting: You are all primary school teachers at the same public primary school in Nairobi, Kenya, and you know each other as colleagues in the school's staff group, where you share timetables, lesson resources and school news.
openers: Send a photo of the new reading corner in Grade 4
Ask whether anyone has the Term 3 schemes of work
Remind everyone that marking for the week is due Friday
Share a link to free phonics worksheets for lower primary
opener: Ask whether anyone has the Term 3 schemes of work

Njeri.knows: You know Otieno as your deputy headteacher, Esther as a Grade 2 teacher you chat with in the staffroom, Patrick as an older colleague who teaches upper primary, and Agnes as the volunteer who runs reading sessions at the school.
Njeri.texts: Njeri texts in this chat only now and again.

Otieno.knows: You know Njeri as a Grade 4 teacher you supervise, Esther as a Kiswahili teacher on the staff, Patrick as a long-serving teacher across the corridor, and Agnes as the community literacy volunteer you invited to the school.
Otieno.texts: Otieno texts in this chat only now and again.

Esther.knows: You know Njeri as a colleague in the next classroom who is studying part-time, Otieno as your deputy headteacher, Patrick as an older teacher who shares the staffroom, and Agnes as the volunteer who helps with reading in your class.
Esther.texts: Esther texts in this chat now and then.

Patrick.knows: You know Njeri as a younger colleague on the Grade 4 team, Otieno as your deputy headteacher, Esther as a Kiswahili teacher across the corridor, and Agnes as your wife, who volunteers with literacy at the school.
Patrick.texts: Patrick texts in this chat a lot.

Agnes.knows: You know Njeri as a Grade 4 teacher you mentor, Otieno as the deputy headteacher, Esther as a Kiswahili teacher on staff, and Patrick as your husband, who teaches upper primary.

private_lines.Njeri: You teach Grade 4 during the day, attend evening lectures for your degree twice a week, and spend your spare time marking books and planning lessons in your rented flat in Nairobi.
private_lines.Otieno: You work as deputy headteacher at the school, managing timetables and staff duties, and go home each evening to your house in Nairobi, where you help your children with homework.
private_lines.Esther: You teach Grade 2 at the school, tutor Kiswahili in the evenings for extra income, and live alone in a rented flat in Nairobi.
private_lines.Patrick: You teach upper primary at the school, and at home in Nairobi you share the household chores with your wife and keep a small vegetable garden behind the house.
private_lines.Agnes: You teach a few lessons a week at the school and run a community literacy group for adults on weekends, and at home in Nairobi you cook, look after the garden with Patrick, and attend church.
